module_title: Food Chains, Food Webs, and Energy Flow
introduction: In nature, 'who eats whom' determines how energy flows through the environment. This flow is governed by strict thermodynamic laws that dictate the structure of all life on Earth.

core_concepts.title: Food Chain
core_concepts.description:
A linear sequence of organisms through which nutrients and energy pass as one eats another. 
Example: Grass $\rightarrow$ Grasshopper $\rightarrow$ Frog $\rightarrow$ Snake $\rightarrow$ Eagle.

core_concepts.title: Food Web
core_concepts.description: In reality, food chains are never isolated. A network of interconnected food chains is called a Food Web. **Rule of Thumb: The larger and more complex a food web is, the more STABLE the ecosystem will be.**

core_concepts.title: Lindeman's 10% Law
core_concepts.description:
Proposed by Raymond Lindeman (1942). It states that during the transfer of energy from one trophic level to the next, **only 10% of the energy is stored as flesh and passed on**. The remaining 90% is lost to the environment as 'Heat' during respiration and daily activities. 
Example: If Grass has 10,000 Joules $\rightarrow$ Grasshopper gets 1,000 J $\rightarrow$ Frog gets 100 J $\rightarrow$ Snake gets 10 J $\rightarrow$ Eagle gets only 1 J.

core_concepts.title: Direction of Energy Flow
core_concepts.description: The flow of energy in an ecosystem is strictly **'Unidirectional'** (One-way). Energy flows from the Sun to plants, then to animals. It NEVER flows backward from animals to the Sun.

important_entities.name: Limit on Trophic Levels
important_entities.significance: Because 90% of energy is lost at every step (10% Law), very little energy remains after 4 or 5 trophic levels. This is why food chains naturally cannot be infinitely long.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The Biggest Exam Trap: Energy flow is always **'Unidirectional'**. However, the flow of nutrients (like Carbon, Nitrogen, Phosphorus) is always **'Cyclic'** (they go from soil to plants, to animals, and back to the soil via decomposers).

mnemonics_and_tricks.trick_title: The Burden of the Top Predator
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The animal at the very top of the food chain (like a Tiger or Eagle) gets the LEAST amount of energy from a single meal, which is why top carnivores must roam large areas and hunt frequently.

exam_strategy_tips: A favorite State PCS/UPSC question: 'Who proposed the 10% law of energy transfer in an ecosystem?' Answer: Raymond Lindeman.
